note.title: ⚖️ Chow Hang-tung|鄒幸彤
note.desc: Barrister and Hong Kong Alliance vice-chair who kept the Tiananmen vigil alive after it was banned — jailed across a string of national-security and assembly cases, and in 2026 for inciting subversion.

pageProps.body:
⚖️ Chow Hang-tung|鄒幸彤

Related: 🕯️ Tiananmen Vigil | Faces of the Crackdown | Hong Kong Alliance | 8964 Museum | The Hong Kong 47 | ⚖️ Jimmy Lai

Chow Hang-tung at a June 4th commemoration, wearing a "毋忘" ("never forget") headband. Photo: Iris Tong / Voice of America, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

Chow Hang-tung (鄒幸彤, born 24 January 1985) is a Hong Kong barrister and the last public leader of the Hong Kong Alliance, the group that for three decades organised the city's June 4th candlelight vigil for the victims of the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. When the vigil was banned in 2020 and the Alliance's chair and vice-chair jailed in 2021, Chow became its convenor and its most defiant voice — urging Hongkongers to remember June 4th on their own, and answering each prosecution from the dock rather than with silence. She has been behind bars since September 2021, convicted across a series of cases that together trace the dismantling of Tiananmen memory in Hong Kong.

From geophysics to the Bar

Chow studied geophysics at the University of Cambridge, taking BA, MSc and MPhil degrees, and worked briefly for an NGO before abandoning doctoral studies and returning to Hong Kong in 2010 to study law. She completed her PCLL at the University of Hong Kong and was called to the Bar in 2016. She joined the Alliance's standing committee and became its vice-chair in December 2015, combining a human-rights legal practice with the annual work of staging the Victoria Park vigil.

A string of prosecutions

As the vigil was criminalised and the Alliance dismantled, Chow was prosecuted in case after case — several of them for simply calling on people to commemorate.

CaseChargeOutcome
2020 vigilInciting/taking part in an unauthorised assembly (the first banned June 4th vigil)Convicted 13 Dec 2021 — 12 months
2021 vigilInciting others to take part in an unauthorised assemblyConvicted 4 Jan 2022 — 15 months (partly consecutive). Acquitted on appeal Dec 2022, but the acquittal was overturned and the conviction restored in 2024
"Foreign agent" refusalFailing to comply with a police demand for information (the Alliance disputed that it was a "foreign agent")Convicted Mar 2023 — 4.5 months
Incitement to subversionConspiring to incite subversion under the National Security Law (the Alliance's "end one-party dictatorship" platform)Convicted 21 Aug 2026; sentenced 11 Sept 2026 — 7 years 3 months

The incitement-to-subversion case is the most serious. On 21 August 2026, three national-security judges convicted Chow, Alliance chair Lee Cheuk-yan and the organisation itself of spreading the call to "end one-party dictatorship" (結束一黨專政). On 11 September 2026 the court jailed Chow for 7 years 3 months — the heaviest term of the three (Lee received 7 years; founding member Albert Ho 5 years 2 months) — placing the case in the higher "serious nature" band despite acknowledging it involved "no violence or the threat of violence." With about five years already served on remand, she has roughly two years left to serve. The fuller story is on the Hong Kong Alliance and 8964 Museum pages.

Defiance from the dock

Chow has repeatedly represented herself, turning her hearings into public statements rather than pleas for leniency. At her January 2022 sentencing she argued she had meant only to "incite others not to forget June 4," not to gather a crowd; the judge called that "simply unbelievable" and barred her from reading the memoirs of Tiananmen victims in mitigation. At her 28 August 2026 mitigation hearing she declined to plead for a lighter sentence, saying the conviction itself showed that "pursuing democracy is a crime," and at the 11 September sentencing she offered no mitigation at all. In custody she has kept up the fight in smaller ways — in August 2024 launching a legal challenge after prison authorities withheld four books they deemed "anti-authority."

Recognition abroad

As her prosecutions mounted, Chow became an internationally recognised symbol of Hong Kong's shrinking freedoms. In 2023 alone she was awarded the Franco-German Prize for Human Rights and the Rule of Law, the CCBE Human Rights Award from the Council of Bars and Law Societies of Europe, and South Korea's Gwangju Prize for Human Rights — honours accepted on her behalf while she remained in a Hong Kong jail. The UN, rights groups and several governments have repeatedly called for her release. In September 2026 the European Parliament named her among the political prisoners it demanded be freed, in a resolution (459–12) urging EU sanctions on the Hong Kong officials responsible (see Hong Kong Alliance).

noteIndex.title: SHKO(Save Hong Kong Online)
noteIndex.body:
[![Great Extinction](/assets/extinctions.jpeg)](/notes/wx39zljncctue32jn06u29u/) 
> (_Courtesy: [Hong Kong Freepress](https://hongkongfp.com/2021/11/28/explainer-over-50-groups-gone-in-11-months-how-hong-kongs-pro-democracy-forces-crumbled/), 2021_) 

SHKO (Save Hong Kong Online) is a community-driven project dedicated to preserving the rapidly disappearing websites and online resources of Hong Kong’s civil society and independent media since 2019. In response to the sweeping shutdowns caused by political changes in Hong Kong, we aim to safeguard digital heritage before it vanishes. This project is anonymous, open source, and supported by a global network of contributors.

While most sites in our archive were forced offline due to Hong Kong’s political deterioration, it’s important to note that [[RFA Cantonese|sites.rfa_cantonese]] is the only site here closed not because of Hong Kong’s situation, but due to internal political decisions in the United States.

Explore our full list of preserved sites and archives on the [Collections page](/notes/wx39zljncctue32jn06u29u/).

Recent work: documenting the [[Hong Kong Fire 2025|hong-kong-fire-2025]] tragedy at Wang Fuk Court (168 dead, ongoing probes into flammable mesh/foam, bid-rigging, and a judge-led review), including activism, timeline, and investigation subpages; and the [[⚖️ Jimmy Lai case|faces-of-the-crackdown.jimmy-lai]] — Apple Daily founder sentenced to 20 years under the National Security Law (Feb 2026), with coverage of press freedom impact and international response; and [[🎵 Glory to Hong Kong|glory-to-hong-kong]] — the 2019 protest anthem and the 2024 court order that made it the first song banned in Hong Kong since the 1997 handover; and [[📕 Book Censorship under the NSL|book-censorship]] — how Hong Kong criminalised the printed word, from the banned Sheep Village children's-book trilogy (whose speech-therapist authors were jailed for sedition) and purged public libraries to the 2026 bookshop raids; and [[🗽 Statues & Monuments|statues]] — how Hong Kong's public monuments to Tiananmen and the 2019 protests (the Pillar of Shame, the Goddess of Democracy, Lady Liberty) were removed, seized as police evidence, and driven into exile abroad; and [[⚖️ The Hong Kong 47|hong-kong-47]] — the largest National Security Law case, in which 45 pro-democracy figures were jailed for up to 10 years over a 2020 opposition primary election; and [[🕯️ Tiananmen Vigil|tiananmen-vigil]] — the thirty-year Victoria Park candlelight vigil for the 1989 crackdown, the largest June 4th commemoration on Chinese soil, now banned and its organisers jailed; and [[✊ Faces of the Crackdown|faces-of-the-crackdown]] — a human index to the publishers, students, unionists and clergy jailed, exiled or tried under the National Security Law; and [[🎬 Films & Documentaries|films]] — the protest movement on film, a decade of documentaries and features (Ten Years, Revolution of Our Times, the Joshua Wong doc) now largely banned or unshowable in Hong Kong, gathered with their trailers.

## Goals
- To preserve as much information as possible before its disappearance during Hong Kong's great transition
- To illustrate a viable method that everyone can use to help preserve online heritage with no pains
- To demonstrate global collaborations to save local digital heritages with best practices

## Quick Facts

We are working on over dozens of [[websites or online causes | sites]] in Hong Kong in the past two decades which has been forced to shutdown or at the brink of disappearing. We'd welcome anyone help [[contribute | participation]] to the content and/or [[sponsor | sponsorship]] our program to sustain it together. 

Examples:
- [[sites.appledaily]] (Extincted)
- [[sites.inmediahk]] (In Danger)
